chunks: From him, from al-Nadhr, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the loan for use (ariyyah), so he said: 'There is no liability (guarantee) on the borrower of a loan for use if it perishes, provided he was trustworthy (did not exceed the normal limits of use).'

key_terms.الْعَارِيَّةِ: Loan for use (gratuitous bailment of an item)
key_terms.مَأْمُونًا: Trustworthy / Not exceeding normal usage / Not negligent
key_terms.مُسْتَعِيرِ: The borrower (one who borrows for use)

ai.seo_question: What is the borrower's liability if a borrowed item is lost or destroyed in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'ithm' (liability) in gratuitous bailment, distinguishing it from paid rental by exempting the borrower from compensation if the item perishes due to normal use or accident, provided they were 'ma'mun' (trustworthy and did not exceed the agreed scope). This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and the presumption of innocence in financial transactions, reflecting the broader ethical framework of trustworthiness in Islamic commerce.
